hero.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during testing at Cape Canaveral
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Launch Complex 36 in Cape Canaveral, Florida on Thursday night at 9 p.m. ET. The massive fireball destroyed the launchpad seconds after the scheduled test began, with the explosion visible as an orange glow across Florida's space coast and even reported by residents in South Carolina over 100 miles away.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed that all employees were safe and accounted for following the incident. The company described the explosion as "an anomaly" and said it was already investigating the cause. Bezos tweeted that it was a "very rough day" but expressed confidence the company would rebuild and return to flying.

The explosion represents a significant setback for Blue Origin's ambitions in the commercial space industry. Just two days before the test, NASA announced that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three planned uncrewed lunar missions this year to begin construction of a $20 billion moon base. The New Glenn rocket is the vehicle Blue Origin intends to use for these critical NASA missions, which are part of the Artemis program to return humans to the moon.

The incident threatens NASA's timeline for lunar base development. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency would conduct a full evaluation of the program's schedule following the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," Isaacman posted on social media. "We will work with our partners to support a thorough investigation of this anomaly, assess near-term mission impacts, and get back to launching rockets."

This explosion comes amid a string of recent setbacks for Blue Origin. Last month, a payload from the New Glenn's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit, and the Federal Aviation Administration temporarily grounded the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the vehicle to return to flight.

Blue Origin is competing with SpaceX across multiple fronts. Both companies have built large facilities at Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions with NASA. For the Artemis program specifically, Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander will compete against SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System to determine which system will carry astronauts to the lunar surface during the Artemis IV mission planned for 2028.

The explosion was widely felt across Florida's space coast, with shockwaves shaking homes in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach. Flames continued burning at the launchpad more than two hours after the blast. Emergency officials reported no threat from fumes or other hazards, though the extent of damage to the launch facilities remains under assessment.

cards.headline: Russia preparing large-scale attack on Ukraine, Zelenskyy warns
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president said Russia is organizing a major new strike in the coming hours.
cards.body:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia is preparing big attacks on Ukraine within the next 24 hours. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told his American counterpart Marco Rubio that US nationals should evacuate Kyiv.

The warning comes as Russia continues offensive operations across multiple fronts. Zelenskyy's statement indicates Ukrainian forces are bracing for intensified strikes, though he did not specify the expected targets or nature of the anticipated attack.

cards.headline: Trump meeting on Iran yields no deal announcement
cards.teaser: President Trump met with advisers but did not announce a final decision after US and Iran reportedly agreed to a framework.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers following official confirmation that the US and Iran had agreed to a framework for a deal. However, the meeting concluded without any deal announcement.

The framework agreement between the two countries represents progress in negotiations, though Trump has not yet committed to proceeding forward.

cards.headline: Uganda closes border with Democratic Republic of Congo as Ebola outbreak grows
cards.body:
Uganda has shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo following a growing outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the neighboring country. The closure represents an effort to prevent further spread of the virus, which has already reached Uganda.

Health officials in the Democratic Republic of Congo have reported 65 deaths from the outbreak, with 246 suspected cases identified primarily in Ituri province. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed that laboratory testing detected the Ebola virus in 13 of 20 samples analyzed. Uganda's health ministry has confirmed cases within its own borders, including a 59-year-old man who died in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC. Ugandan officials have reported seven confirmed cases of the virus.

The Bundibugyo strain is distinct from the more common Zaire strain responsible for previous major outbreaks in the region. This particular virus has no licensed vaccine currently available, unlike the Zaire strain. The Bundibugyo virus was first identified in Uganda in 2007, with previous outbreaks occurring in 2007 and 2012.

Officials express particular concern about the outbreak's location in Ituri province, which borders Uganda and South Sudan. The region contains mining towns characterized by significant population movement, making disease control efforts challenging. The World Health Organization's director general, Dr. Jean Kaseya, emphasized that rapid regional coordination is essential given the high movement of people between affected areas and neighboring countries.

The World Health Organization has estimated the outbreak's death rate at between 30 and 50 percent among confirmed cases. The organization's head arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo to support containment efforts and called for an immediate ceasefire in the eastern DRC, warning of a "catastrophic collision of disease and conflict" that is outpacing response efforts.

Ebola spreads through direct contact with body fluids of infected individuals, including blood and vomit, as well as contact with dead bodies during funeral preparations. The disease is characterized by severe illness and high fatality rates.

Several factors contribute to regular Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to health experts. Close human contact with animal reservoirs, likely bats or primates, plays a significant role. Additional concerns include movement between rural and urban environments, tropical climate conditions, and extensive rainforest coverage.

The Democratic Republic of Congo has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976. The border closure is expected to remain in place while health authorities assess the outbreak's scope and implement containment measures. The Africa CDC has convened an urgent meeting with authorities from affected countries and pharmaceutical companies to coordinate response efforts.

cards.headline: SEC proposes repealing climate disclosure rule for companies
cards.teaser: The Securities and Exchange Commission moved to eliminate a rule requiring companies to report greenhouse gas emissions and climate risks.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has proposed repealing a climate disclosure rule that mandates public companies report their greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related financial risks. The rule was adopted under the Biden administration to provide investors with standardized information about how environmental factors could affect company performance.

The repeal would eliminate these reporting requirements, reversing the previous administration's push to establish consistent climate risk disclosure standards across publicly traded companies.

cards.headline: Space Force awards SpaceX $4.16 billion contract for missile-tracking satellites
cards.teaser: SpaceX won a contract to build a satellite network for tracking airborne targets as part of the Space Force's Golden Dome program.
cards.body:
The U.S. Space Force awarded SpaceX a $4.16 billion contract to develop satellite sensors for tracking airborne threats from space. The satellites will support the Pentagon's "Golden Dome" defense system, enhancing the military's ability to detect and monitor targets.

This contract is part of a broader relationship between SpaceX and the Space Force. According to the company's IPO filing, SpaceX generated one-fifth of its 2025 revenue from government contracts, demonstrating the significance of defense work to the company's business.

cards.headline: Louisiana passes congressional map eliminating majority-Black district
cards.teaser: Louisiana lawmakers approved new electoral boundaries that eliminate a majority-Black congressional district, giving Republicans an additional House seat.
cards.body:
Louisiana Republicans passed a new congressional map that eliminates one of the state's two majority-Black districts. The move follows a U.S. Supreme Court ruling that found the previous map unconstitutional. The redistricting is expected to provide Republicans with an additional House seat.

The new boundaries significantly alter Louisiana's congressional representation and reshape the state's political landscape ahead of future elections.

cards.headline: Russia warns Europe to expect more drone incidents after strike on Romanian building
cards.teaser: A Russian official issued a warning to Europe following a drone crash into a Romanian apartment building.
cards.body:
A Russian drone struck a residential apartment building in Romania, drawing condemnation from NATO and the European Union. Romanian officials said the drone was likely hit by air defences over Ukraine, causing it to change course before hitting the building.

Following the incident, a Russian official warned European countries to expect additional drone incidents in the future. NATO member states criticized Russia over the strike on the Romanian residential block.

cards.headline: Russia preparing large-scale attack on Ukraine, Zelenskyy warns
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president said Russia is organizing a major new strike in the coming hours.
cards.body:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia is preparing big attacks on Ukraine within the next 24 hours. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told his American counterpart Marco Rubio that US nationals should evacuate Kyiv.

The warning comes as Russia continues offensive operations across multiple fronts. Zelenskyy's statement indicates Ukrainian forces are bracing for intensified strikes, though he did not specify the expected targets or nature of the anticipated attack.

cards.headline: European Union to release billions withheld from Hungary after Orban's election defeat
cards.teaser: The EU is set to unlock 16 billion euros previously frozen over corruption and rule of law concerns.
cards.body:
The European Union is unlocking €16.4 billion in frozen funds for Hungary following the election of a new prime minister. The leader, who took office less than three weeks ago, represents a shift in the country's political direction.

The EU had previously withheld the funds over concerns about corruption and rule of law violations. The release reflects optimism about Hungary's commitment to anti-corruption measures and policies aligned with EU standards.

cards.headline: Spain's Prime Minister Sanchez faces pressure amid corruption investigations
cards.teaser: Multiple probes targeting colleagues and family members threaten the survival of Spain's leader after eight years in office.
cards.body:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is navigating a political crisis stemming from corruption investigations involving his colleagues and relatives. After eight years leading the government, these probes have intensified pressure on his administration.

Despite the mounting scandals, Sanchez has signaled his intention to remain in office and continue his leadership role.

cards.headline: Ghana passes law criminalizing LGBTQ+ identification
cards.teaser: Parliament approved legislation that makes same-sex acts and identifying as gay, lesbian or transgender punishable by jail time.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament has passed legislation that criminalizes same-sex conduct and LGBTQ+ identification. The new law imposes jail sentences for individuals engaging in same-sex acts, which were already prohibited under existing law.

The bill represents an expansion of criminal penalties in the West African nation, now targeting not only same-sex behavior but also identification as gay, lesbian, or transgender.

cards.headline: Japan tightens visa rules, forcing some foreign curry shop owners to leave
cards.teaser: New immigration policies under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are affecting foreign business owners who have established themselves in Japan.
cards.body:
Foreign owners of curry shops in Japan are being forced to leave the country under new visa restrictions implemented by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government. The policy changes are part of a broader immigration crackdown affecting business owners who had put down roots in the country.

The visa rule changes specifically impact foreign entrepreneurs operating small businesses. Some curry shop owners who had established themselves in Japanese communities now face departure under the tightened immigration policies.

hero.headline: US military strike in Pacific kills three, pushing drug interdiction death toll past 200
hero.body:
A US military strike on a suspected drug smuggling boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean killed three people, bringing the cumulative death toll from such operations above 200 since September.

US Southern Command announced the latest strike, describing those killed as "male narco-terrorists" without providing evidence or identifying the terrorist organizations allegedly operating the vessel. The command stated that "intelligence confirmed the vessel was transiting along known narco-trafficking routes in the Eastern Pacific and was engaged in narco-trafficking operations."

The strike represents the third attack this week as the Trump administration intensifies its campaign against what it calls "narcoterrorism." A similar boat strike on Monday in the Caribbean Sea killed two people. No US military forces were harmed in the latest operation.

The administration has significantly ramped up these military operations in recent weeks. According to available reports, more than 190 people had been killed in such strikes before this latest attack, with the new deaths pushing the total past 200.

However, the military operations have drawn sharp criticism from human rights advocates and legal experts. Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International have characterized the strikes as "unlawful extrajudicial killings," arguing that the US military is conducting executions without proper legal process. The American Civil Liberties Union has described the Trump administration's assertions about its targets as "unsubstantiated, fear-mongering claims."

A central issue fueling the debate is the lack of transparent evidence. US Southern Command has not provided definitive proof that the vessels being struck are involved in drug trafficking operations. The military has also not disclosed the nationalities of those killed or the specific locations where the boats were operating when struck.

The operations target vessels in the eastern Pacific and Caribbean, regions long used as corridors for drug smuggling operations attempting to move narcotics northward. The Trump administration frames the military action as part of a broader counter-narcotics strategy using military force in international waters.

The legality of these strikes remains contested among experts and human rights organizations both in the United States and internationally. Critics argue that targeting individuals based solely on intelligence assessments, without providing evidence or due process, violates international law and fundamental human rights principles.

US Southern Command has not responded to requests for additional details about targeting procedures or the evidence used to identify vessels as drug smuggling operations. The military continues to describe those targeted as operators of designated terrorist organizations while declining to specify which groups are involved.

The mounting death toll underscores the expanding scope of US military involvement in drug interdiction operations at sea, even as questions persist about oversight, transparency, and the legal authority for such strikes.

cards.headline: Trump meeting on Iran yields no deal announcement
cards.teaser: President Trump met with advisers but did not announce a final decision after US and Iran reportedly agreed to a framework.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers following official confirmation that the US and Iran had agreed to a framework for a deal. However, the meeting concluded without any deal announcement.

The framework agreement between the two countries represents progress in negotiations, though Trump has not yet committed to proceeding forward.

cards.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge blocked the renaming and ordered the removal of Trump's name from the Kennedy Center building.
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered the Kennedy Center to remove President Trump's name from the building. The ruling also blocked Trump's plans to close the performing arts center for two years of extensive renovations, requiring it to remain open.

Trump responded angrily to the decision. The court's order represents a significant setback to Trump's efforts to reshape the Kennedy Center's operations and identity.

cards.headline: Louisiana passes congressional map eliminating majority-Black district
cards.teaser: Louisiana lawmakers approved new electoral boundaries that eliminate a majority-Black congressional district, giving Republicans an additional House seat.
cards.body:
Louisiana Republicans passed a new congressional map that eliminates one of the state's two majority-Black districts. The move follows a U.S. Supreme Court ruling that found the previous map unconstitutional. The redistricting is expected to provide Republicans with an additional House seat.

The new boundaries significantly alter Louisiana's congressional representation and reshape the state's political landscape ahead of future elections.

cards.headline: Three convicted in Spokane ICE protest conspiracy case
cards.teaser: A federal jury found three protesters guilty of conspiracy charges stemming from an ICE demonstration in Spokane.
cards.body:
A federal jury convicted three people, including an army veteran, for their role in an ICE protest in downtown Spokane. The case tested legal strategies pursued by the Trump administration against protesters.

The three defendants were found guilty on conspiracy charges. The prosecutor in the trial issued a statement following the verdict, though the case outcome marks a significant legal precedent for how protest activity is prosecuted.

cards.headline: Bondi testifies on Epstein files, points to Blanche and Patel
cards.teaser: Former Attorney General Pam Bondi told lawmakers that redaction errors occurred in the Epstein files release and shifted responsibility to others.
cards.body:
Former US Attorney General Pam Bondi defended her handling of Epstein files during congressional testimony about a month after her removal by President Trump. When pressed by lawmakers over the document release, Bondi attributed redaction errors to Todd Blanche and Kash Patel.

Her testimony redirected scrutiny toward Blanche, positioning him as a focal point for Democratic investigators examining how the files were managed and released to the public.

cards.headline: Trump's physician says president is in excellent health
cards.teaser: The White House released a medical report stating Trump is fully fit to serve, though his doctor recommended weight loss and more exercise.
cards.body:
President Trump's physician declared the 79-year-old president in excellent health and fully capable of serving. The doctor recommended that Trump lose weight and exercise more.

The White House departed from standard practice by declining to release a comprehensive medical report. Instead, the physician offered a general assessment of the president's health status without the detailed documentation typically provided.

cards.headline: China's biotech industry gains ground in drug development
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China drew attention at an international oncology conference as the country's biotechnology sector expands.
cards.body:
Chinese clinical trials are receiving international recognition, as demonstrated by their prominence at a major oncology conference in Chicago. This visibility reflects the advancing capabilities of China's biotechnology sector.

The growth of China's drug development has prompted concerns in the U.S. about shifting competitive advantage in biotechnology. Substantial investments in the biotech sector have expanded China's clinical trial activity and research output, establishing the country as an increasingly significant player in global medical research.

cards.headline: Universal Music Group rejects Bill Ackman's $64 billion takeover bid
cards.teaser: The music company declined a takeover proposal from investor Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, saying it undervalued the company.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group turned down a takeover proposal from billionaire investor Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Capital Management. The investment firm had valued the music company at approximately $64 billion to $65 billion.

Universal Music Group, home to major recording artists, determined that Ackman's offer did not adequately reflect its value and rejected the bid.

cards.headline: Fire at Penn Station disrupts Amtrak and NJ Transit service
cards.teaser: An Amtrak train fire near Penn Station in New York caused service suspensions and injured five people.
cards.body:
A fire on an Amtrak train near Penn Station disrupted rail service for commuters and injured five people. The fire occurred during rush hour, affecting both NJ Transit and Long Island Rail Road passengers.

Amtrak and NJ Transit reduced service at Penn Station through the weekend following the incident. Amtrak service later resumed through the station, though the fire caused significant delays and commuter chaos during the evening rush period.

cards.headline: Stock markets reach record highs as oil prices decline
cards.teaser: Major stock indexes closed at record levels as investors responded to falling oil prices and potential progress on an Iran agreement.
cards.body:
Stock markets hit record closing levels, with the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and Nasdaq all finishing at fresh highs. Technology stocks drove the rally, with Dell among the top performers. The gains extended the market's winning streak as investors responded positively to artificial intelligence stocks and diplomatic developments.

Oil prices declined sharply following reports of progress in U.S.-Iran ceasefire negotiations. Brent crude futures fell 1.3% on Friday to around $92, marking a 19% drop since the end of April. The steepest monthly decline since 2020 reflects investor optimism about a potential end to Middle East tensions.

hero.headline: Proposed rules would let government cancel research grants at any time
hero.body:
The federal government has proposed new rules that would allow officials to cancel research grants at any point without cause. The changes would also make peer review optional and introduce political screening of grant applications for prohibited topics.

The proposal marks a significant shift in how the government awards and manages funding for scientific research. Under current practice, peer review serves as the standard method for evaluating research proposals, with panels of independent scientists assessing applications based on scientific merit.

The new framework would give political staff authority to screen grant applications before approval. Reviewers would look for topics the administration has designated as forbidden, though the proposal does not specify which subjects would be restricted.

The cancellation provision represents the most sweeping change in the proposed rules. Grant recipients currently receive funding commitments for the duration of approved research projects, typically spanning multiple years. The new policy would eliminate that protection, allowing the government to terminate funding at any stage of a research project.

Researchers depend on multi-year funding commitments to plan long-term studies, hire staff, and purchase equipment. Sudden cancellations could leave projects incomplete and researchers without the resources to finish work already underway.

The optional peer review provision would permit the government to award grants based on criteria other than scientific evaluation. Peer review was developed to ensure that taxpayer funds support the most promising research, with decisions made by experts in each field rather than by administrators.

The proposal applies to federally funded research across multiple agencies. Federal grants support work at universities, research institutes, and private laboratories throughout the country. In 2025, the government distributed billions of dollars in research funding across fields including medicine, physics, computer science, and climate research.

The rules have not yet taken effect. The government typically allows a comment period before finalizing policy changes of this scope, giving researchers and institutions time to respond to the proposal.

cards.headline: SpaceX receives $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: The company disclosed that government contracts already accounted for one-fifth of its 2025 revenue.
cards.body:
SpaceX disclosed $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts as part of its IPO financial filings. The company revealed that government contracts accounted for one-fifth of its 2025 revenue, underscoring the significant role federal spending plays in its business.

The Space Force agreements represent a major portion of SpaceX's federal relationships, which extend beyond the military to include NASA and other government agencies.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks deportation of Ebola-exposed Americans
cards.teaser: The Trump administration had planned to send exposed individuals to Kenya rather than specialized US facilities.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked the Trump administration's plan to send Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya for quarantine. The ruling prevents the transfer of individuals who may have been exposed to the virus during an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Instead of allowing exposed Americans to return home, the White House confirmed it was building a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya. Some experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning to the US undermines treatment efforts.

cards.headline: Indian court ruling on Google ad practices draws founder criticism
cards.teaser: The decision prompted renewed complaints from company founders about how Google handles trademarked keywords in advertising.
cards.body:
An Indian court ruling on Google's advertising practices has reinvigorated criticism of the platform from company founders. The decision addresses how Google handles trademarked keywords in its ad system, particularly whether advertisers can bid on competitors' brand names to trigger their own ads in search results.

Legal experts believe the ruling could push platforms to reconsider their approach to trademarked terms in advertising. The case has drawn support from founders who have long raised concerns about Google's ad business practices.

cards.headline: Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm tease new laptop processors
cards.teaser: The companies have released cryptic messages hinting at Nvidia's N1X laptop chips.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are jointly teasing an upcoming announcement about Nvidia's new Arm-powered laptop processors. The Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts on X both posted "A new era of PC," with Arm following suit with its own teaser messages.

The announcement is expected at Computex this weekend. Microsoft also teased new Surface hardware alongside the processor reveal, with Surface chief Pavan Davuluri hinting at "something new" for developers, including what appears to be a curved display design.

cards.headline: Researchers warn AI code tools may not improve code quality
cards.teaser: Coders are increasingly unwilling to work without AI assistance, but researchers question whether the technology produces better results.
cards.body:
Programmers are refusing to work without AI coding assistants, even as researchers raise concerns about the quality of AI-generated code. The tools help coders write software faster, but studies suggest speed may come at the expense of code quality.

Researchers warn that relying on AI for code production could create problems for developers in the long term. While the tools accelerate the writing process, they may not be producing more reliable or maintainable software.

cards.headline: Southeast Asia's largest known dinosaur identified in Thailand
cards.teaser: The newly discovered species measured 89 feet in length.
cards.body:
Scientists have identified the largest dinosaur ever discovered in Southeast Asia from fossils found in Thailand. The specimen measured 89 feet long, making it the biggest known dinosaur species from the region.

Fragmentary fossils can make it difficult to determine the exact size of ancient creatures. Researchers rely on comparisons with more complete specimens and measurements of individual bones to estimate total body length.

hero.headline: Washington Nationals fire team official after hidden-camera video shows comments on player
hero.body:
The Washington Nationals fired a team executive after a hidden-camera video showed the official making comments about the team's treatment of a Catholic pitcher. The video allegedly captured the executive saying the team avoided featuring a conservative player on social media.

Sources confirmed the executive was let go following the release of the footage. The video appears to show the official discussing what sources described as religious discrimination against the player.

The incident has drawn attention from federal authorities. The team now faces a potential Department of Justice probe based on the alleged admission of religious discrimination captured in the video.

The executive's comments centered on a pitcher whose religious beliefs and political views were cited as reasons for limiting his visibility in team promotional materials. The hidden-camera recording captured statements about internal team decisions regarding player representation on social media platforms.

The Nationals have not publicly detailed the circumstances of the executive's departure or the content of the video. The team also has not commented on the potential federal investigation.

The matter raises questions about how professional sports organizations handle players with differing political and religious viewpoints. Religious discrimination in employment is prohibited under federal civil rights law.

The timing of the executive's termination came shortly after the video surfaced publicly. The speed of the dismissal suggests the team moved quickly once the footage became known.

The player at the center of the situation has not been publicly identified by name in most reports. The nature of the social media decisions and how long they were in effect also remains unspecified in available reports.

The potential Justice Department involvement indicates the matter may extend beyond an internal team personnel decision. Federal investigators would need to determine whether civil rights violations occurred based on the executive's alleged statements and any corresponding team actions.

cards.headline: Teenager Joao Fonseca defeats Novak Djokovic at French Open
cards.teaser: Brazilian 19-year-old rallied from two sets down to eliminate Djokovic in the third round at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Brazilian teenager João Fonseca staged a remarkable comeback to defeat Novak Djokovic 4-6, 4-6, 6-3, 7-5, 7-5 in a five-set epic at the French Open. After Djokovic claimed the first two sets on Court Philippe-Chatrier, the 19-year-old Fonseca rallied to win the final three sets in a grueling four-hour match.

The victory eliminates the 39-year-old Djokovic from the tournament and denies him a 25th Grand Slam title. Fonseca's triumph marks a breakthrough moment for the rising Brazilian star and signals his arrival among tennis's elite competitors.

cards.headline: Thunder's Jalen Williams ruled out for Western Conference Finals Game 7
cards.teaser: Oklahoma City will play without Williams as the series against San Antonio reaches its deciding game.
cards.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder will face the San Antonio Spurs in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday without Jalen Williams. The decisive matchup will take place in Oklahoma City, with the winner advancing to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks.

The Spurs forced Game 7 with a dominant 118-91 victory in Game 6, powered by Victor Wembanyama's 28 points and 10 rebounds. Williams' absence represents a significant loss for the Thunder in the elimination game.

cards.headline: Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby placed 40 bets on Indiana football while playing for the Hoosiers
cards.teaser: Sorsby wagered nearly $90,000 during his college career, including dozens of bets on his own team in 2022.
cards.body:
Brendan Sorsby, now the quarterback at Texas Tech, made at least 40 bets related to Indiana football in 2022 while he was on the Hoosiers roster. Sorsby admitted to wagering nearly $90,000 throughout his college career.

Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire is pushing for Sorsby's reinstatement as the NCAA investigates the matter. The revelation comes amid broader debates about student-athlete gambling and enforcement of NCAA betting rules. The case has intensified discussions about appropriate penalties for players who wager on games involving their own teams.

cards.headline: Pentagon requires troops to meet weight standards for free tickets to White House UFC event
cards.teaser: Military personnel must meet fitness criteria to attend the UFC fight being hosted at the White House for the president's birthday.
cards.body:
The Pentagon is recruiting troops to attend a UFC fight at the White House, but service members must meet weight standards to receive free tickets. Internal memos show the fitness requirements for attendance at the event.

The UFC fight is being hosted at the White House for the president's birthday. The eligibility criteria have raised questions about the selection process for attendees. Safety concerns about hosting a combat sports event at the White House have also been raised by commentators including Joe Rogan.

cards.headline: Sacramento makes pitch for MLB expansion team
cards.teaser: City leaders are pursuing a Major League Baseball franchise with investors already expressing interest.
cards.body:
Sacramento is making a formal push to become an MLB expansion city, with local leaders pitching the idea of placing a team in West Sacramento. The effort has attracted attention from potential investors, with some prominent names already involved in preliminary discussions.

Fans in the region have expressed support for bringing a major league team to the area. Sacramento joins Vancouver and other western cities exploring expansion opportunities. MLB has not announced any timeline or cities under consideration for expansion, but multiple markets are positioning themselves as potential homes for new franchises.

cards.headline: NASCAR runs full race weekend at Nashville
cards.teaser: Cup Series, O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, and Truck Series all compete at Nashville Superspeedway.
cards.body:
NASCAR is holding a complete weekend of racing at Nashville, with the Cracker Barrel 400 headlining the Cup Series schedule. The O'Reilly Auto Parts Series and Truck Series are also running races at Nashville Superspeedway.

The weekend features both veteran drivers and rising stars competing across the three series. Full television coverage is available throughout the weekend for all races. The Nashville event represents one of the major stops on the NASCAR calendar as the season progresses.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the film editor who won an Oscar for her work on Star Wars, died Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80. The family's attorney confirmed she died of cancer.

Lucas was one of three editors to share an Academy Award for editing the 1977 film Star Wars, directed by her former husband George Lucas. She also edited several influential films of the 1970s, including Taxi Driver.

Lucasfilm posted a statement mourning her death. The company described her as a brilliant storyteller and a trailblazer in the film industry.

Marcia Lucas shaped the final cut of Star Wars, helping to create one of the most successful films in cinema history. Her editing work contributed to the pacing and narrative structure that made the science fiction epic a cultural phenomenon.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas built a distinguished career editing films during a transformative period in American cinema. Her work on Martin Scorsese's Taxi Driver in 1976 demonstrated her range and skill across different genres and filmmaking styles.

She was married to George Lucas during the production of the original Star Wars trilogy. The couple divorced in 1983, and Marcia Lucas largely stepped away from film editing in the years that followed.

Her death represents the loss of a key figure from the team that created Star Wars. While George Lucas is widely recognized as the franchise's creator, Marcia Lucas's contributions as editor were critical to shaping the film that audiences saw in theaters.

The film editing community has long recognized her talent and influence. Her Oscar win for Star Wars acknowledged work that involved assembling footage, refining the story's rhythm, and making creative decisions that enhanced the finished film.

Lucas died following a battle with metastatic cancer. She spent her final days in Rancho Mirage, a city in Riverside County, California. She was 80 years old at the time of her death.

cards.headline: Music Executive Clive Davis Hospitalized in New York
cards.teaser: The 94-year-old music industry executive was hospitalized in New York City on Friday evening following a respiratory issue.
cards.body:
Clive Davis was hospitalized in New York City on Friday evening. The 94-year-old music executive was admitted following a respiratory issue.

Davis has been a prominent figure in the music industry for decades. He has worked with numerous artists and led major record labels throughout his career.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Concert Dates
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is canceling the remainder of his 2026 concert schedule due to health issues.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli announced Friday that he is canceling the remainder of his 2026 concert dates to focus on his health. The 92-year-old singer, known for his dedication to performing, shared the news on social media.

Valli expressed his apologies to fans who had purchased tickets to the canceled shows.

cards.headline: Multiple Artists Drop Out of Freedom 250 Concert Series
cards.teaser: Over half of the performers scheduled for the Great American State Fair have withdrawn from the Trump-backed Freedom 250 concerts honoring America's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
Multiple artists have withdrawn from the Freedom 250 concert series scheduled for July 6 to commemorate America's 250th anniversary on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. At least seven of the nine featured musical acts dropped out within 48 hours of the lineup being announced.

Among those who canceled are Martina McBride, Morris Day, Young MC, and Bret Michaels. Michaels cited a deteriorating atmosphere surrounding the event and threats as reasons for his withdrawal. The concert series is organized by the Trump administration.

cards.headline: A24 Horror Film Backrooms Earns $10 Million in Previews
cards.teaser: The debut film from 20-year-old director Kane Parsons has already grossed more than $10 million before its nationwide release.
cards.body:
Backrooms, the directorial debut of 20-year-old Kane Parsons for A24, has grossed over $10 million in preview screenings and is now playing nationwide. The film stars Chiwetel Ejiofor as Clark, an architect-turned-furniture store owner who discovers a mysterious portal to the "backrooms" in his basement. Renate Reinsve co-stars as his therapist, Dr. Mary Kline, whom Clark struggles to explain his discovery to.

The horror film explores the terror of liminal spaces and sinister architecture as its central concept. Based on a YouTube series that inspired the movie, Backrooms also features Mark Duplass, Finn Bennett, Avan Jogia, and Lukita Maxwell in its cast.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Urges Governor Candidates to Support Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman called on candidates to back uncapped tax incentives for film and television production in California.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman urged candidates for governor on Friday to support uncapped tax incentives for film and television production. She appeared outside Radford Studios with entertainment industry figures who support her mayoral campaign.

Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon were among those who joined Raman. She said California must ensure that Hollywood remains a center for production. The governor election is scheduled for Tuesday.

cards.headline: DJ John Summit Announces 2026 Arena Tour
cards.teaser: The DJ is bringing his CTRL ESCAPE tour to arenas across the United States and Canada this fall.
cards.body:
John Summit announced a 2026 tour with stops in arenas across the United States and Canada. The CTRL ESCAPE tour is scheduled for the fall.

Tickets for the tour are now available. Summit is a DJ who has built a following in the electronic music scene.

hero.headline: White House releases memo saying Trump in excellent health after physical
hero.body:
The White House released a memo on Friday stating that President Trump remains in excellent health following his annual physical examination at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center earlier in the week.

Trump visited the military hospital on Tuesday for the routine evaluation, where he underwent cardiac, neurological, dermatologic and other medical examinations. His physician documented the findings and concluded that Trump remains fit to serve as president.

The White House delayed releasing the physician's assessment until several days after the physical took place. Presidential health evaluations are typically disclosed through summary memos rather than complete medical records, a practice that allows administrations to share general health information while keeping specific medical details private.

The memo provided an overall assessment of Trump's health status without including detailed findings from individual examinations conducted during the visit. The physician's statement centered on the conclusion that the president's health supports his continued service in office.

Annual physicals are routine medical evaluations that all sitting presidents undergo. Walter Reed serves as the primary medical facility for presidents and other high-ranking government officials.

However, independent physicians have raised questions about observations not addressed in the official assessment. According to reports, medical professionals who have not directly examined Trump have noted recurrent bruises on his hands and swelling in his legs. These concerns have emerged from outside observers commenting on the president's appearance.

The timing of the memo's release on Friday evening followed the completion of the various medical examinations at the military hospital and the preparation of the physician's written assessment.

The White House's approach to disclosing presidential health information reflects a longstanding practice in American politics. Rather than releasing comprehensive medical documentation, administrations provide summary statements that offer the public general information about a president's health status while maintaining privacy around specific test results and clinical details.

The memo's focus on Trump's fitness for office aligns with how previous administrations have handled similar evaluations. The physician's determination that the president remains in excellent health and fit to serve represents the official medical conclusion regarding his ability to carry out presidential duties.

The release of the health assessment came as part of routine maintenance of presidential medical records and public disclosure practices that have evolved over several decades of White House operations.

cards.headline: US military kills three in strike on suspected drug boat in eastern Pacific
cards.teaser: U.S. Southern Command said the vessel was traveling along known narco-trafficking routes and being operated by designated terrorist organizations.
cards.body:
The U.S. military carried out another strike Friday on a boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean accused of drug smuggling, killing three men. This marks the third attack this week in an ongoing campaign against suspected drug trafficking vessels in the region, bringing the overall death toll from these operations above 200 people.

U.S. Southern Command announced the strike, stating the vessel was engaged in narco-trafficking operations and operated by a designated terrorist organization. The boat was transiting along known drug trafficking routes in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Pam Evette over Nancy Mace in South Carolina governor race
cards.teaser: President Trump backed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the contest, calling her an America First Patriot who never wavered.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed a GOP challenger to Rep. Nancy Mace's campaign for South Carolina governor on Friday, backing Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the contest. The president lauded Evette as an America First Patriot who never wavered in a Truth Social post Friday evening.

Trump wrote that Evette is a good friend, fighter, and winner. The endorsement places Trump in opposition to Mace, a Republican congresswoman seeking the governorship.

cards.headline: Southcom commander meets with Cuban military officials
cards.teaser: Gen. Francis L. Donovan joined Cuba's First Deputy Minister of the Chief of the General Staff and other leaders near Naval Station Guantanamo Bay.
cards.body:
The head of U.S. Southern Command met with senior leaders of the Cuban military on Friday amid heightened tensions between the two countries. Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan joined Cuba's First Deputy Minister of the Chief of the General Staff Roberto Legra Sotolongo and other leaders near Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, Southcom announced.

The meeting occurred as tensions between the U.S. and Cuban governments have increased. Southcom oversees U.S. military operations in Central and South America and the Caribbean.

cards.headline: Judge reopens Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit for further scrutiny
cards.teaser: A federal judge sided with intervenors who said a settlement to create an anti-weaponization fund tainted the case.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. The decision came after intervenors argued that a settlement agreement to establish an "anti-weaponization" fund had improperly influenced the case. Trump and the Department of Justice had previously agreed to voluntarily dismiss the suit in exchange for creating the fund.

The judge's ruling allows for additional examination of the case proceedings. The intervenors' concerns about how the settlement arrangement affected the litigation were the basis for reopening the case.

cards.headline: Talarico leads Paxton by three points in Texas Senate poll
cards.teaser: Forty-seven percent of likely general election voters backed state Rep. James Talarico compared with 44 percent for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.
cards.body:
The Democratic candidate in the Texas Senate race holds a slight edge over his Republican opponent in a new poll released Friday. State Rep. James Talarico garnered support from 47 percent of likely general election voters, while Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton received 44 percent in the Texas Public Opinion Research survey.

The three-point margin indicates a competitive race as the two candidates move toward the general election following the primary runoff.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary Bessent endorses putting Trump on $250 bill
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent said the proposed currency would commemorate the U.S. semiquincentennial featuring President Trump.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the White House is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill featuring President Trump's portrait to celebrate the nation's 250th anniversary of independence. The proposal would require changing federal law that currently prohibits living people from appearing on U.S. currency.

Bessent announced at a White House news conference that the Treasury Department has already begun preparing for the possibility of issuing the new currency. Democrats have vowed to block the move.
